text:
Matias Maccelli's Islanders season has come in two pieces. He started with a five-game point streak, then left the Oct. 17 game in Toronto with a lower-body injury and missed nine games. Since returning on Nov. 12 he has three assists in two games, both Islanders wins.

The role is the story. He has been on the ice for 84% of the Islanders' power-play chances, up from 31% last season in Toronto, and 4 of his 9 points have come there. Nine points in 10 games is a strong start for a player who had 39 in 71 last year.

Some of it will cool. New York has scored 5.1 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own chance creation is modest at 0.52 expected goals per 60. He is a passer first: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 92nd percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, with 20% of his setups crossing the royal road, the pass across the middle that moves a goalie side to side. Ten games is small; the power-play job is real.
headline: Maccelli is back and running the power play
